haiku-low.q1: Once per deploy, by a single migrate task run after the image build and before any new-release instance exists. The live (previous) release must keep working on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using it has been retired, meaning its env was scaled to 0 in the retire step of the deploy that replaced it.
haiku-low.q3: All four instances must pass /healthz three times in a row, then the smoke suite must pass, within the 10-minute gate deadline. If not, abort: the candidate is scaled to 0 and the prod listener is untouched.
haiku-low.q4: The prod listener is flipped in one change, all at once with no weighting, to the candidate's target group. That moment is T (switched_at). The previous env keeps running.
haiku-low.q5: Over 1% 5xx on the public listener in a rolling 5-minute window during T to T+15, or an engineer triggering the rollback job. Rollback repoints the listener to standby, scales the new env to 0, alerts. Migrations and schema are left alone.
haiku-low.q6: Until T+30, when the previous colour is scaled to 0. After that there is no quick flip back; a problem is handled by a normal deploy of the previous release through the full pipeline.
haiku-low.q7: A failed transaction rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, its invalid index is dropped, committed additive changes stay, and the index is retried next deploy. The run stops, live keeps serving, and the deploy finishes as failed.
haiku-low.q8: The live colour is read from where the public listener forwards, the only lasting record, and copied into run variable live_colour. The other colour becomes new_colour and is scaled to 0 if needed. No state file exists.
haiku-low.q9: The concurrency group deploy-catalog-web. Other deploys queue behind it. The run holds it through to finish, and CI releases it if the run dies, so the group is held for the full run.
haiku-low.q10: Through the internal test listener on port 8443, reachable only from CI, which is pointed at the candidate's target group. Smoke runs after health passes, while users remain on the old colour.
haiku-low.q11: A single migrate task run by the pipeline from the new image against shared Postgres. Instances do not migrate on boot, which keeps it to once per deploy.
haiku-low.q12: After an abort or rollback the new colour is scaled to 0 and left idle. The next deploy goes into whichever colour has 0 instances. If scale-down failed, the next deploy's live-colour step scales it to 0 first.

sonnet.q1: Migrations run after the build/check and the candidate-independent steps but before any instance of the new release exists (before candidate bring-up and the flip). The currently live colour (previous release) must keep working on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still used the thing has been retired (its env scaled down in the retire step of the deploy that replaced it). The build step's check rejects drops, renames, or type changes.
sonnet.q3: All 4 candidate instances must pass the LB /healthz check (every 10s, 3 times in a row), then the smoke suite must pass via the test listener, all within gate_deadline (10 minutes after bring-up). If health or smoke fails or the deadline runs out, abort (candidate scaled to 0, prod listener untouched, finish as failed).
sonnet.q4: A single, all-at-once change of the prod listener to forward to the candidate's target group (no weighting). In-flight requests on the old env just finish since it keeps running.
sonnet.q5: Automatic rollback: 5xx on the public listener over 1% in a rolling 5-minute window during the 15-minute watch from T. Rollback points the listener back at the standby colour's target group, scales the new env to 0, and alerts. It never touches migrations (schema stays as is). Then finish as failed.
sonnet.q6: Until retire at T+30 (scaling the previous colour to 0). Between T+15 and T+30 the standby is still up, and an engineer can trigger the pipeline's rollback job. After retire there is no quick flip back; a rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release through the full process.
sonnet.q7: If the table/column transaction fails, it rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, the invalid index is dropped, committed table/column changes stay (additive), and the failed index migration is not recorded so the next deploy retries it. Either way the run stops, the new side is never started, live keeps serving, and the run finishes as failed.
sonnet.q8: By looking at where the public listener forwards; that is the only lasting record (no state file). The run copies it into run variables live_colour and new_colour; the other colour receives the new release. Variables exist only for the run's duration.
sonnet.q9: The concurrency group (deploy slot/lock) named deploy-catalog-web; other deploys queue. It is held from the start of the run through finish (and for a rollback until the listener is back on the old side); released at finish, or automatically by CI if the run dies.
sonnet.q10: Via the internal test listener on port 8443 (reachable only from CI), pointed at the candidate's target group, after health passes; the prod listener still points at the old env.
sonnet.q11: A single `migrate` task run from the new image against the shared Postgres. Once per deploy is ensured because instances do NOT migrate on boot; only that task does.
sonnet.q12: Both abort and rollback scale the new/candidate colour to 0 instances (abort: candidate; rollback: new env, plus alert). The next deploy treats whichever side is at 0 instances as the one to deploy into; its live-colour step also scales the non-live colour to 0 if scale-down had failed.
